title: Native PC, Amiga and Spectrum reconstruction discovery
summary: Review 28 pinned repositories: add 18 projects and record ten deferrals or duplicates.
notes: Root personally searched 25 repository queries across C64, ZX Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS/Windows. Screened against current main at 5452 projects. Reviewed 28 available pinned trees, primary documentation and selected implementation/build files; four additional candidates could not be read and were not promoted. No qualifying new Atari ST or CPC addition established in these searches. Source and modern host platforms remain distinct. Partial source recovery is not called a complete game; binary parity claims are attributed and bounded. No candidate programs, dependency installers or game images executed. Only exact UTF-8 proof bodies are sealed; larger and CP949 implementation files are linked and selectively inspected. No worker, branch or PR used.

sources.reason: Recreates Manic Miner platforming and key collection as a competitive game for up to four players. Native Godot player, conveyor, death/respawn and winner logic; intentionally changed multiplayer rules, not binary reconstruction.
Java2D/Swing reimplementation with teachers, pupils, shield collection, blackboards and safe-code objectives. Teacher class models sight, patrol, dazing and code reveal using semantic objects.

Native Go/Ebitengine remake with typed players/enemies, original collision boundary rules, weapons, formations and campaign data extracted from a user-supplied Amiga ADF. Selected engine code implements game rules rather than a guest CPU loop.

Small partial decompilation containing the engine interface, string helper and threading source. Inspected interface defaults and Win32 string implementation; no recovered game logic or whole-game implementation claimed.

Reconstructs Windows 95 build 950.6 utilities/modules including Notepad, Welcome, Winver, Telephony and resource/mixer helpers. C/assembly sources and binary-comparison tooling exist; this is not a complete Windows operating-system reconstruction.

Reverse-engineers Dungeon Siege and Legends of Aranna assets, with Tank archive decompression, RAW image conversion and partial ASP/SNO geometry import. Selected RAW handler uses decoded image headers and mip surfaces.

Reconstructed Ex Machina / Hard Truck Apocalypse engine and drivers. Weapon-group source links original RVAs to semantic C++ objects and containers; renderer, input and sound DLLs have their own source trees.

Recovers the real-mode loader, protected-mode game image, containers/codecs/audio and match subsystems into typed C libraries and an SDL3 host engine. Ball-pairing source uses semantic actor/vector records rather than guest-register execution.
Rebuilds the Polish Sammy Suricate release from recovered Acknex WDL rules and game data. Deterministic Rust simulation and semantic enemy patrol logic feed Bevy or SDL2/GLES frontends.

Recovers six 2002 Pocket PC card games from Windows CE ARM executables: Klondike, Spider, Golf, War, Hearts and Spades. Browser Hearts source links original functions to native rule/opponent logic; SDL2 C Klondike is also retained.

Portable C++20 game logic with Godot GDExtension presentation. Recovered race AI helpers cite original addresses and operate on vectors and vehicle objects. Menus, driving, opponents and combat are explicitly partial.
Reimplements Windows 95 CD Collection build .022 in C++20/SDL3 for Apple Silicon, including semantic city simulation, resource parsing, original-derived map rendering and a new UI with SCURK editors.
Recovered managed Retro Engine source including player positioning/collision, stages, audio and scripting with assembly token/RVA annotations; Windows launcher and phone API stubs accompany it.

Reusable headless DOS runner for observing original programs during remake verification. Go API exposes instruction-bounded execution, memory reads, snapshots, indexed pixels and call interception; explicitly executes original x86 code.

Bash recreation of Ramsberg and Berntsson's DOS text adventure, with parser commands, inventory, room transitions and puzzle-state logic. This is the parody The True Story, not Melbourne House's Hobbit interpreter.
Recreates the Korean PC shooter with Allegro/DJGPP, native projectile/movement routines and original-style presentation. Only Stage 1 is currently available.
Single-page Canvas recreation of Greg Kuperberg's 1982 PC CGA Paratrooper, with helicopters, paratroopers, gun firing and scoring rules implemented in JavaScript.

Recreates Dave Hughes' 2018 Spectrum Bean Brothers with Godot prototype and native Z88DK C/Spectrum Next version. Custom collision logic has parallel GDScript/C implementations rather than depending on Godot physics.

Partial 3D reinterpretations of Spectrum games in a jMonkeyEngine arcade. Source exists, but original game reconstruction fidelity/coverage is not established; retain as a remake-scope lead rather than a source-recovery addition.

Repository describes a Jumping Jack remake, but inspected main.cpp renders an animated player/zombie example at fixed positions. Title-specific platform/gap rules are not established; defer until game logic exists.
Pinned tree contains only a design DOCX, with no implementation source. Do not promote an Android port on repository description alone.
C64 assembly learning prototype of Amiga BIP with sprite/HUD/input scaffolding. Movement routine is explicitly unfinished and main game rules are not established; retain for later review.

Mixed collection: five native TypeScript rebuilds coexist with six 6502 translations running on a modeled C64; music also uses 6502/SID emulation. Do not label the whole root native. Needs execution-path audit distinguishing game logic, sound-only emulation and full translated game paths.

C port intentionally keeps a flat mem[] at original addresses and an original-address to C-function registry. Extensive bounded parity claims do not settle execution-architecture classification; retain for targeted audit rather than falsely claim either a conventional native semantic port or a general CPU interpreter.

Early generic driving/renderer prototype with Bullet btRaycastVehicle and a newly modeled track. README says original core features remain a future goal and physics may need replacement; title-specific reconstruction not yet established.
GitHub identifies this as a fork of already tracked dj--alex/m2k; no independently reviewed divergent reconstruction established.
GitHub identifies this as a fork of already tracked adamenkov/jet-story; no independently reviewed divergent reconstruction established.
GitHub identifies this as a fork of tracked rusarh/exolon-esl. README credits Sergey Erokhin and original Bitbucket project; avoid duplicate promotion.
